title: Netherlands – Insurance services – WGA Eigenrisicodrager verzekering Gemeente Oude IJsselstreek
description: Ingeval van WGA eigenrisicodragerschap is de werkgever rechtstreeks verantwoordelijk voor de financiering van de aan de werkgever toe te rekenen WGA uitkeringen (tot maximaal 10 jaar na toekenning). Tevens gaat de re-integratieplicht na toekenning van een WGA uitkering over van UWV naar werkgever. Ter afdekking van de risico’s bij WGA eigenrisicodragerschap wenst Opdrachtgever een WGA Eigenrisicodrager Verzekering af te sluiten. Het betreft hier een private verzekering t.b.v. financiering van de aan de werkgever toe te rekenen WGA Vast en WGA flex uitkeringen. Opdrachtgever heeft op peildatum 1 september 2026 in totaal 362 werknemers in dienst. De verwachte WIA loonsom in 2026 bedraagt circa € 20,5 miljoen. Voor de inschatting van het risico en het vaststellen van de condities stelt de Aanbestedende dienst een beveiligd Excel document ter beschikking met geanonimiseerde personeelsgegevens, opgave zieke medewerkers en WIA instroom. Dit Excel bestand kan opgevraagd worden bij de gemeente Oude IJsselstreek door een verzoek hiertoe in te dienen op het e-mailadres aanbesteding@oude-ijsselstreek.nl . Dit Excel bestand wordt alleen verstrekt aan belangstellenden met een vergunning van de AFM voor het uitvoeren van het verzekeringsbedrijf conform de Wet Financieel Toezicht (of daarmee vergelijkbare wet- en regelgeving in het buitenland) en die een WGA eigenrisicodrager verzekering in het productassortiment voeren.

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.4 - How can technology improve both the efficiency and the patient experience in NHS transport, starting with renal services?â
description: With over 273,000 people in Scotland living with Stage 3-5 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), including 2,000 receiving dialysis treatment, and demand expected to increase fivefold over the next decade, improvements to dialysis transport across NHS Scotland are urgently needed. Dialysis journeys account for more than 40% of all non-emergency patient transport activity, costing 9.1 million GBP annually. Yet current arrangements can be inconsistent, creating avoidable pressures for patients, providers and NHS services. NHS Scotland is seeking innovative, patient-centred and sustainable solutions that improve reliability, efficiency and patient outcomes, while reducing administrative burden and delivering better value for money.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.3 - How can we use technology to demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy business practices?
description: Zero Waste Scotland is seeking an innovative technology solution that helps businesses demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy practices and attract investment. Existing assessment tools often overlook benefits including (but not limited to) supply chain resilience, resource security, customer retention and reduced exposure to market shocks. We are looking for an intuitive, evidence-based tool that integrates the wider benefits into business and investment decisions, while generating insights to inform future support and policy development. The solution should build business and investor confidence, help accelerate adoption of circular practices and support Scotland's transition to a sustainable, circular economy.

title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?
description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isnât readily available (or isnât trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotlandâs Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 â 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individualâs âcircle of supportâ. This âcircle of supportâ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services â and if possible, create a âfeedback loopâ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.4 - How can technology improve both the efficiency and the patient experience in NHS transport, starting with renal services?â

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services â and if possible, create a âfeedback loopâ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: CivTech 12 - Challenge 12.3 - How can we use technology to demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy business practices?
description: Zero Waste Scotland is seeking an innovative technology solution that helps businesses demonstrate the commercial value of circular economy practices and attract investment. Existing assessment tools often overlook benefits including (but not limited to) supply chain resilience, resource security, customer retention and reduced exposure to market shocks. We are looking for an intuitive, evidence-based tool that integrates the wider benefits into business and investment decisions, while generating insights to inform future support and policy development. The solution should build business and investor confidence, help accelerate adoption of circular practices and support Scotland's transition to a sustainable, circular economy.

title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?
description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotlandâs child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?
description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenantsâ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.

title: Lukituksen uusiminen (16 kohdetta)
description: Lukituksen uusiminen (16 kohdetta) MEKAANINEN LUKITUS Sarjoituksen kohteena on 16 asuinkiinteistöä. Kohteiden mekaaninen lukitus uusitaan Abloy Easy - järjestelmällä. Sylinterit uusitaan, vanhat lukkorungot ja helat säilytetään. Urakoitsija on velvollinen tutustumaan kohteisiin omatoimisesti ennen tarjouksen antamista ja varmistamaan lukituskaavioiden ajantasaisuus. Jätekatokset, piharakennukset, postilaatikot yms. lukitukset kuuluvat urakkaan kohteissa, joissa nämä ovat ennestäänkin lukittuja. Urakkaan kuuluu lisäksi lukkojen telkien ja avainpesien (käyttölukot, varmuuslukot, pitkäsalvat) voitelu ja ruuvien kiristys. Muut tarvittavat korjaukset tehdään tarvittaessa lisätyönä. Urakka sisältää kaikki työt ja tarvikkeet valmiin lopputuloksen saavuttamiseksi sekä uuden lukituskaavion. Uuden lukituskaavion lisäksi laaditaan yhteisistä tiloista päivitetyt sijoituspohjapiirrokset tilaajalle. Lukituskaaviot ja uudet avaimet toimitetaan avainhallintapisteisiin (huoltoyhtiö/lukkoliike). Lukostojen laajuus on vanhan lukoston mukainen seuraavin huomautuksin: - avaimia 3 kpl / avaintyypit asunto, lehdenjakaja, reitti, kerhohuone jne. - huoltoavaimia 7 kpl, joista 1kpl toimitetaan KTL1E järjestelmän avainsäilöön - yleisavaimia 7 kpl - kaikki avaimet leimataan (yksilöity tunnus) - lukoston käytettävissä olevan reservin tulee olla mahdollisimman laaja Avaimet toimitetaan avainhallintapisteeseen viimeistään 14vrk (2 viikkoa) ennen sovitun asennusajan aloittamista TELETILOJEN SARJOITUS KTL1E Lisäksi kaikkien kiinteistöjen yhteiset teletilat sarjoitetaan KTL1E-järjestelmään ja rakennuksien ulkoseinään asennetaan KTL1E järjestelmän avainpesä (mikäli tyhjiä paikkoja ei ole, kuuluu avainsäilöputken seinään poraaminen myös urakkaan). Yhteisiä teletiloja ovat talojakamot, alijakamot, kerrosjakamot ja yhteisiin tiloihin asennetut kytkentäpaikkoja tai telelaitteita sisältävät muut ovelliset kotelot ja rasiat. KTL1E-avainsäilöputkeen toimitetaan 1kpl kohteen huoltoavaimia. Kaksi avainsäilön käyttöavainta toimitetaan muiden avaimien mukana avainhallintapisteeseen. KTL1E järjestelmän liittymismaksuista vastaa tilaaja. TIEDOTTAMINEN Tiedotteet töiden aloittamisesta (kohdekohtaisesti) tehdään yhteistyössä tilaajan kanssa viimeistään 3 viikkoa ennen asennustöiden aloittamista. Asukkailla on oltava tiedotteen saatuaan vähintään 14 vrk aikaa hakea avaimet avainhallintapisteestä ennen töiden aloittamista. Tiedotteiden jakamisesta vastaa tilaaja. URAKKA-AIKA Urakka-aika sovitaan erikseen, kuitenkin siten, että kaikki asennukset ovat valmiina maaliskuun 2027 loppuun mennessä.,

title: Finland – Adult and other education services – Työntekijäksi teollisuuteen! Teollisuuden osaamis- ja täydennyskoulutukset työvoimakoulutuksena/ Pohjoisen Keski-Suomen työllisyysalue
description: Pohjoisen Keski-Suomen työllisyysalue pyytää tarjouksia tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden ja HILMA-ilmoituskanavassa julkaistun hankintailmoituksen työvoimapalveluiden järjestämislain (380/2023) luvun 7 mukaisista työvoimakoulutuksista, joiden olisi tarkoitus alkaa arviolta loppuvuonna 2026. Tarjouspyyntö ja sen liitteet ovat kaikilta osin tarjoajaa sitovia. Hankinta toteutetaan puitejärjestelynä. Puitejärjestelyyn valitaan osa-alueittain enintään yksi palveluntuottaja. Puitejärjestelyyn valinta oikeuttaa palveluntuottajan vastaanottamaan tilaajan tekemiä koulutustilauksia sopimuskauden aikana, mutta ei anna palveluntuottajalle oikeutta ennalta määrättyyn koulutusmäärään tai hankinnan arvoon. Hankinta koostuu kahdesta (2) pääteemasta, jotka kilpailutetaan tarjouspyynnössä erillisenä osakokonaisuutena. Nämä pääteemat ovat: - Kone- ja tuotantotekniikka - Prosessiteollisuus Hankinnan määrä on yhteensä 2500 opiskelijatyöpäivää (otp) sopimuskaudella. Koulutuksesta maksetaan toteutuneiden opiskelijatyöpäivien mukaan. Hankinta sisältää myös tulospalkkion. Hankinnan arvioitu sopimusaika on 1.12.2026 - 31.12.2027. Hankintaan liittyy optiomahdollisuus kahteen (2) yhden (1) vuoden pituisiin sopimuskausiin kolmen (3) vuoden kulussa alkuperäisen hankintasopimuksen laatimisesta. Option käyttöönotosta päättää tilaaja. Option käyttöönotosta ilmoitetaan palveluntuottajalle viimeistään kolme kuukautta ennen optiokauden alkua. Hankinnassa voidaan sopia tarvittaessa lisäostosta, joka on enintään 50 % alkuperäisen hankinnan arvosta. Lisäostoa voidaan käyttää kullakin sopimuskaudella opiskelijatyöpäivä määrien ylityksiin tai sopimuskaudella alkaneiden koulutusten jatko-osuuksiin (ns. hännät). Tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevassa palvelukuvauksessa on tarkemmat tiedot palvelun sisällöstä. Tarjouspyynnössä esitetyt hankintamäärät ovat arvioita, eivätkä ne muodosta hankintayksikölle määräostovelvoitetta. Palvelun siirtyminen, peruuntuminen tai hankkimatta jättäminen ei aiheuta hankintayksikölle korvausvelvollisuutta.

title: Psychological Risk Assessment Services (Psychologist) – Ontario Region
description: Psychological Risk Assessment Services (Psychologist) This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, for Joyceville Complex, Collins Bay Complex, Bath Complex, Millhaven Institution, Warkworth Institution, Beavercreek Complex, Grand Valley Complex, and the Regional Treatment Centre at Millhaven Institution and Bath Institution in the Ontario Region. Trade agreement: This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) has a requirement to obtain professional psychological risk assessment services to support offender case management, decision-making, and risk management activities. Services include the completion of structured and unstructured psychological risk assessments, professional opinions, and related documentation in accordance with CSC policies, legislation, and professional standards of practice. Objectives: The objective of this requirement is to ensure CSC has timely access to qualified psychological expertise to conduct risk assessments that support safe, effective, and evidence-based correctional decision-making. Deliverables: The Contractor must provide professional psychological services, including but not limited to: • Completion of psychological risk assessments as requested by CSC; • Preparation of written psychological reports and professional opinions in the format required by CSC; • Documentation of findings in CSC-approved systems; • Participation in consultations or clarification discussions related to completed assessments, when required. Clarification discussions refer to consultations with CSC to explain, amend, or respond to questions related to completed psychological risk assessments. All deliverables must meet accepted professional standards, be delivered in English, and comply with CSC security, privacy, and operational requirements. Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. title: Modular Wind Power for Northern Operations
description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness levels (TRL) 1-9 can be submitted to this challenge. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/016 - Modular Wind Power For North Operations The Department of National Defence and Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) are seeking innovative solutions to develop modular, stand-alone wind-powered electric generator systems that can be easily transported, deployed, and maintained in remote northern locations to provide reliable, clean energy under extreme cold, high-wind, and icing conditions. Background & Context The demand for electrical power and space heating in the Canadian Subarctic and High Arctic is fulfilled almost exclusively with diesel-fired generators. The DND/CAF is seeking to reduce reliance on fossil fuels for the generation of electrical power in the North to minimize operational, logistical, and environmental burdens. Wind turbines suitable for DND/CAF operations are in limited use in the North, as existing installations tend to fall outside the desired capacity range. While small units that deliver up to 6 kilowatts (kW) have been deployed in some communities, and commercial turbines typically exceed 1 megawatt (MW), there is a critical gap in the 25–100 kW range—an ideal scale for remote DND sites. In addition, northern operating conditions present major technical and environmental hurdles that must be overcome before wind turbines can be fully exploited as a source of alternative energy. Canada's far North and Arctic regions are characterized by seasonally frozen ground, deep snow, rugged terrain, permafrost, and extreme temperatures that can reach –60 degrees Celsius (°C), with frequent high winds of 80–120 kilometers per hour (km/h). Ice rimming of wind turbine blades further threatens performance and efficiency. Innovative approaches are therefore needed to adapt conventional wind-powered electric generator designs to withstand these harsh northern conditions and operate effectively under both low and high wind scenarios. Climate change adds additional complexity, as thawing and refreezing permafrost can cause buildings and foundations to sink, shift, or crack. While not the primary focus of the challenge, consideration must be given to the design of the foundations to keep the turbines level and stable despite seasonal ground movement. There is a need for wind-powered electricity generators that are logistically efficient, easy to deploy, and maintainable in isolated northern locations. Many DND/CAF sites exist in remote areas or within small Arctic communities that have limited or no road access and must be reached by alternative means of transportation such as barges or heavy-lift aircraft. Consequently, new systems must feature modular designs that can be transported and assembled on site with minimal heavy-lift equipment by non-technicians using commonly available tools. To ensure sustained operation, proposed solutions should use readily available parts, be serviceable by local tradespeople, and operate with minimal human intervention once deployed. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Provide a design for a wind-powered electrical generation system in the 25–100 kW range, incorporating details of the structural, mechanical, electrical, and control elements required. • Provide integration and operational demonstration plan(s), showing how the wind-powered electric generator system can function in remote northern locations and operate and withstand northern environmental conditions, including extreme cold (down to –60 °C), high winds (up to 120 km/h), and icing conditions without intervention. • Integrate with existing electrical power systems or microgrids and must enable coordinated operation with other energy sources and support performance under varying generation and load conditions. • Use a modular design that allows transport by air or ship — ensuring that individual components fit within a standard 20ft sea container with maximum dimensions of 108 in. (2.74 m) wide × 268 in. (6.81 m) long × 96 in. (2.44 m) high and a maximum weight of 24,000 lb (10,886 kg; 10.9 tonnes). • The modular design must enable onsite assembly without the need for heavy lift equipment. • Support maintainability and repairability in northern environments by ensuring the wind powered electric generator system can be serviced using standard mechanical and electrical tools, without reliance on specialized proprietary equipment or manufacturer field support. Desired Outcomes Proposed solutions should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Electromagnetic interference that complies with MIL STD 461G, Department of Defense Interface Standard for the Control of Electromagnetic Interference Characteristics of Subsystems and Equipment. • Foundation design that accounts for Arctic ground conditions, including permafrost, active-layer variation, and freeze-thaw effects, over the intended design life of the generator.

title: RF Data Fusion for Command and Control
description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness levels (TRL) 1-9 can be submitted to this challenge. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/017 - RF Data Fusion for Command and Control The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) are seeking innovative software-based solutions to seamlessly convert, analyze, and fuse real-time, domain-specific, content-rich data transmitted over radio frequency (RF) bearers into a secure, standardized pan-domain Command and Control (C2) format to enhance interoperability and enable timely, data-driven decision-making across all domains and levels of command. Background and context Radio frequency (RF) communications in military operations are inherently bandwidth-constrained and vulnerable to jamming, interference, and environmental effects, making them unreliable in contested environments. To maintain timely and effective support across all warfighting domains, data transmitted over RF bearers should be transformed into compact, structured messages, such as eXtensible Markup Language (XML)-based Message Text Formats (MTF) or other machine-readable schemas. Such messages should be optimized for transmission over tactical networks including Low Frequency (LF), Very Low Frequency (VLF), High Frequency (HF), Ultra High Frequency (UHF), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM). This approach enables resilient, standards-based communication across domains (land, air, maritime, cyber, and space) and functional services (e.g., Joint Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (JISR), medical, logistics), in line with doctrinal requirements for pan-domain operations. CAF tactical messaging remains largely dependent on legacy systems. These systems are inflexible, poorly suited to machine-to-machine exchange, and increasingly misaligned with NATO’s shift toward XML-based, data-centric frameworks. CAF operators currently lack integrated, machine-readable messaging systems. As a result, they must manually convert voice, chat, and text inputs into formal military products including orders, situation reports, and Requests for Information (RFIs) to comply with command structures and coalition standards. Modern, pan-domain operations require that doctrinal and technical Information Exchange Requirements (IERs) be met at the speed of operational relevance, with messaging that is interoperable, standardized, and capable of supporting real-time, data-driven decision-making in joint and coalition environments. As NATO, the U.S. Department of Defense, and other Five Eyes partners adopt XML-based, machine-readable messaging frameworks, the CAF is prioritizing alignment with these emerging data models to improve interoperability, operational agility, and mission effectiveness. The DND/CAF are seeking innovative, interoperable, and scalable solutions that will contribute to the development of a next-generation digital military RF messaging and data exchange. Innovators are invited to propose technologies, platforms, or integrated systems. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Be a software-based capability (e.g., standalone application, plug-in, middleware, or service). • Support DND/CAF operations across all domains (land, air, maritime, space, cyber) and functional services (e.g., C2, intelligence, logistics). • Implement structured, standards-compliant messaging (e.g., MTF-XML) and data exchange protocols (e.g., National Information Exchange Model (NIEM), NATO Core Data Framework (NCDF)), with documented interfaces for importing, exporting, and exchanging data using those standards. • Be configurable and modular, supporting Character-Oriented Information Exchange (COIE) processing and designed for future extensibility (e.g., to accommodate emerging or disruptive standards). • Provide documented interfaces and standards-based data exchange mechanisms to support system integration, including use within experimentation, simulation, and wargaming environments. Desired Outcomes The proposed solution should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Operability in Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, and Low Bandwidth (DDIL) environments, with scalability to support evolving mission requirements and force structures. • Enhanced user experience features such as intuitive interfaces, multilingual support, automation of routine workflows, and built-in decision aids. • Standardized, documented integration interfaces (e.g., application programming interfaces (APIs)) to enable integration with at least one Service Management or Service Monitoring tools or platforms (e.g., ServiceNow, Splunk, Dynatrace, Microsoft System Center, Azure Monitor, etc.). • Readiness for future integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities to support data fusion, intelligent message prioritization, and real-time decision support.

title: Sustainable Northern Operations: Water & Waste
description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/018 - Sustainable Northern Operations: Water & Waste The Department of National Defence and the Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) are seeking novel, integrated technologies that enable the CAF to operate Relocatable Transportable Camps (RTCs) independently and sustainably in Arctic and sub-Arctic environments while meeting all applicable Canadian environmental and health regulations. Background and context The CAF’s strategic update Our North, Strong and Free (2024) directs an expansion of military operations in the Canadian North. RTCs deployed in remote Arctic regions must sustain personnel with safe water, sanitation, and waste-handling capabilities while minimizing logistics and environmental risk. In 2023, the IDEaS Pop-Up City contest demonstrated advanced, containerized power-water-waste systems. These prototypes significantly reduced solid-waste mass and potable-water demand but were not tested under Arctic winter conditions. Material brittleness, freezing of fluids, and power-efficiency issues remain key obstacles. This challenge will bridge this gap by developing, and then testing integrated cold-weather water and waste technologies under Arctic winter conditions (e.g., Op NANOOK). The objective of the challenge is to support the development of a proven, deployable, Canadian-made, Arctic-ready water-and-waste system enabling CAF RTCs to operate independently, safely, and sustainably in the North with drastically reduced logistics burden and environmental impact. Essential outcomes Proposed solutions must meet the following requirements: • Integrated capability combining water purification, wastewater treatment and solid-waste reduction suitable for camps of up to 50 personnel. • Use a modular design that allows transport by air or ship – ensuring that individual components fit within a standard 20 ft sea container with maximum dimensions of 108 in. (2.74 m) wide × 268 in. (6.81 m) long × 96 in. (2.44 m) high and a maximum weight of 24,000 lb (10,886 kg; 10.9 tonnes). The modular design must also enable on site assembly without the need for heavy lift equipment. • Treated outputs must meet or exceed Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and Health Canada Drinking-Water Guidelines. • Function continuously in remote northern locations and operate and withstand northern environmental conditions, including extreme cold down to -40°C. • Resource efficiency must be demonstrated through a reduction in resupply volume and frequency (fuel, water, consumables) by at least 75% from baseline (see Table 1 below). • Support maintainability and repairability in northern environments by ensuring that the solution can be serviced using common trades and tools available to CAF in deployed operations in remote areas. Desired outcomes Proposed solutions should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Integrated power. • Operable in extreme heat conditions (up to +40°C). • No manual pre-processing of solid waste. • Recovery and reuse of waste-heat or by-products. • Can be scaled to suit camps of over 50 personnel, up to 1500 personnel. title: Germany – Architectural services for buildings – Vergabe von Planungsleistungen für Architekten „Sanierung und Umbau des denkmalgeschützten Goreth-Hauses“ in Stetten am kalten Markt
description: Die Gemeinde Stetten am kalten Markt (Stetten a.k.M.) beabsichtigt das denkmalgeschützte Goreth-Haus am Schlosshof 2 umfassend zu sanieren und für eine zukünftige öffentliche Nutzung nachhaltig zu ertüchtigen. Neben der denkmalgerechten Instandsetzung der historischen Bausubstanz sind hierzu bauliche Anpassungen im Gebäudeinneren vorgesehen. Das Goreth-Haus befindet sich im Eigentum der Gemeinde. Ein wesentlicher Bestandteil der Maßnahme ist die statische und konstruktive Ertüchtigung des Dachstuhls sowie der Decken über dem Obergeschoss. Das Dachgeschoss soll saniert, jedoch nicht ausgebaut werden. Für die Sanierung des Dachgeschosses liegen bereits grundsätzliche Planungsansätze sowie eine Kostenschätzung aus dem Jahr 2020 für die Kostengruppen 300 (Bauwerk, Baukonstruktionen) und 700 (Baunebenkosten) vor (s. Anlage 2). Der Umfang der erforderlichen gesamten Sanie-rungsmaßnahmen des Goreth-Hauses ist dagegen bislang nur überschlägig untersucht, die in einer ersten Kostenschätzungen in Anlage 3 vorliegt. Maßnahmen zur Gestaltung von Freianlagen sind nicht Gegenstand der vorliegenden Planung.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Zweiphasiger städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Wettbewerb nach RPW 2013 - Produktives Quartier Gutleut-West
description: Gegenstand des Wettbewerbes ist ein städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Entwurf in dem gezeigt wird, wie die Transformation eines gewerblich geprägten Bestandsareals zu einem nutzungsgemischten, klimaangepassten und gemeinwohlorientierten Quartier gelingen kann. In einer Stadt mit hoher Flächennachfrage und begrenzten innerstädtischen Entwicklungsreserven treffen hier Ansprüche unmittelbar aufeinander, die sich andernorts oft räumlich aus dem Weg gehen: Wohnen und Gewerbe, Logistik und Aufenthalt, soziale Infrastruktur und Produktion, Freiraum und Verdichtung. Die entscheidende Frage lautet deshalb nicht, welche Nutzung sich am Ende durchsetzt. Interessanter ist, wie aus dieser Konkurrenz ein Stück Stadt entstehen kann. Aufgabe des Wettbewerbs ist es, eine eigene räumliche Antwort zu entwickeln. Gesucht wird vornehmlich nicht das möglichst vollständige Bild eines irgendwann „fertigen“ Gutleut-West. Gesucht wird vielmehr ein städtebauliches und freiraumplanerisches Gerüst, das Orientierung gibt, ohne Entwicklung einzuschränken. Es soll durch zu entwickelnde Prinzipien Qualitäten sichern und zugleich Spielräume eröffnen – für unterschiedliche Nutzungen, Träger:innen, Eigentümer:innen und Entwicklungszeitpunkte. Die Ausloberin beabsichtigt, unter Würdigung der Empfehlung des Preisgerichts, das mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichnete Team mit der Ausarbeitung des Wettbewerbsergebnisses zu beauftragen. Die Ausloberin wird hierzu ein Verhandlungsverfahren ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb gemäß § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 VgV durchführen. Dabei behält sich die Ausloberin vor, das Verhandlungsverfahren zunächst nur mit dem mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichneten Team durchzuführen. Scheitern diese Verhandlungen oder besteht ein wichtiger Grund, der einer Beauftragung des 1. Preisträgers entgegensteht, werden die weiteren Preisträger zur Teilnahme an den Verhandlungen aufgefordert. Das Wettbewerbsergebnis wird im anschließenden Vergabeverfahren als Zuschlagskriterium mit 60 % gewichtet. Die Rangfolge der Preisträger gemäß der Entscheidung des Preisgerichts wird dabei entsprechend berücksichtigt, d.h. der 1. Preisträger erhält im Kriterium ‚Wettbewerbsergebnis' die höchste Punktzahl, der 2. Preisträger die zweithöchste usw. Die weitere Bearbeitung umfasst den städtebaulichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 51 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone III, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie den freiräumlichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 52 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone III, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie die Erstellung eines "Qualitätshandbuchs". Eine darüberhinausgehende Beauftragung weiterer Planungsleistungen bleibt vorbehalten und ist nicht Bestandteil dieses Auftragsversprechens. Ziel ist die Erarbeitung eines Rahmenplans mit integrierter Freiraumplanung als Vorstufe zum Bebauungsplan nach BauGB sowie als Grundlage für das im Anschluss geplante Konzeptverfahren für die hochbauliche Entwicklung auf den Baufeldern. Die Preisträger:innen verpflichten sich, im Falle einer Beauftragung durch die Ausloberin, die weitere Bearbeitung zu übernehmen und durchzuführen. Im Zuge der Überarbeitung der Wettbewerbsergebnisse treten sie mit der Bürgerschaft und Schlüsselpersonen vor Ort im Rahmen von Dialogformaten in Austausch (z.B. Vorstellung des Wettbewerbs-Ergebnisses, Rückfragenbeantwortung, Aufnahme von Hinweisen für weitere Bearbeitung). Die Beauftragung erfolgt vorbehaltlich des Abschlusses des erforderlichen Vergabeverfahrens, der erforderlichen haushaltsrechtlichen Voraussetzungen, der Eignung des Teilnehmers sowie des Vorliegens eines wichtigen Grundes, der einer Beauftragung entgegensteht. Im Falle einer weiteren Bearbeitung werden durch den Wettbewerb bereits erbrachte Leistungen des Preisträgers bis zur Höhe des zuerkannten Preises nicht erneut vergütet, wenn und soweit der Wettbewerbsentwurf in seinen wesentlichen Teilen unverändert der weiteren Bearbeitung zugrunde gelegt wird.

title: Norway – Works for complete or part construction and civil engineering work – Loppa municipality - Molo - Øksfjord Harbour
description: On behalf of Loppa municipality, tenderers are invited to a competition for improvements to the port conditions in Øksfjord. The General contract (NS 8406) includes the establishment of two new piers, the establishment of a new pumping station, a sewage pipeline and an access road. Dredging the seabed under Molo South is necessary to ensure sufficient geotechnical stability before completion. Dredging masses shall be reused as core masses in the piers and for filling ditches, while any surplus matter is delivered to an approved site. The work shall be carried out with environmental measures such as bubble curtain and turbidity monitoring. The existing sewage pipeline must have been moved and relaid with a new pumping station before sea work starts. The pier North shall be partially established before dredging starts to enable encapsulation of the dredging masses and reduce particle dispersion. The contract includes further filling work, width expansion and extension of Pier North, establishment of a turnaround, as well as concrete work on a new and existing pier. The concrete works are options and include casting breakwater covers, parapets and casting on existing constructions. The builder is free to order all or parts of the optioned concrete works. The execution shall be carried out in accordance with the engineering design documentation and the accompanying drawings. Furthermore, there are option posts for the demolition and re-establishment of approx. 200 metres of existing sewage pipeline on land.

Dabei behält sich die Ausloberin vor, das Verhandlungsverfahren zunächst nur mit dem mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichneten Team durchzuführen. Scheitern diese Verhandlungen oder besteht ein wichtiger Grund, der einer Beauftragung des 1. Preisträgers entgegensteht, werden die weiteren Preisträger zur Teilnahme an den Verhandlungen aufgefordert. Das Wettbewerbsergebnis wird im anschließenden Vergabeverfahren als Zuschlagskriterium mit 60 % gewichtet. Die Rangfolge der Preisträger gemäß der Entscheidung des Preisgerichts wird dabei entsprechend berücksichtigt, d.h. der 1. Preisträger erhält im Kriterium ‚Wettbewerbsergebnis' die höchste Punktzahl, der 2. Preisträger die zweithöchste usw. Die weitere Bearbeitung umfasst den städtebaulichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 51 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie den freiräumlichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 52 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie die Erstellung eines "Qualitätshandbuchs". Eine darüberhinausgehende Beauftragung weiterer Planungsleistungen bleibt vorbehalten und ist nicht Bestandteil dieses Auftragsversprechens. Ziel ist die Erarbeitung eines Rahmenplans mit integrierter Freiraumplanung als Vorstufe zum Bebauungsplan nach BauGB sowie als Grundlage für das im Anschluss geplante Konzeptverfahren für die hochbauliche Entwicklung auf den Baufeldern. Die Preisträger:innen verpflichten sich, im Falle einer Beauftragung durch die Ausloberin, die weitere Bearbeitung zu übernehmen und durchzuführen. Im Zuge der Überarbeitung der Wettbewerbsergebnisse treten sie mit der Bürgerschaft und Schlüsselpersonen vor Ort im Rahmen von Dialogformaten in Austausch (z.B. Vorstellung des Wettbewerbs-Ergebnisses, Rückfragenbeantwortung, Aufnahme von Hinweisen für weitere Bearbeitung). Die Beauftragung erfolgt vorbehaltlich des Abschlusses des erforderlichen Vergabeverfahrens, der erforderlichen haushaltsrechtlichen Voraussetzungen, der Eignung des Teilnehmers sowie des Vorliegens eines wichtigen Grundes, der einer Beauftragung entgegensteht. Im Falle einer weiteren Bearbeitung werden durch den Wettbewerb bereits erbrachte Leistungen des Preisträgers bis zur Höhe des zuerkannten Preises nicht erneut vergütet, wenn und soweit der Wettbewerbsentwurf unverändert der weiteren Bearbeitung zugrunde gelegt wird.

description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE � No. 75N98026R00175 Title: Biobanking, Laboratory Analytics, and Associated Informatics Services for NIH Biorepositories Agency: National Institutes of Health (NIH) Description This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal of abstracts or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified business sources and (2) whether commercial sources and services are available in the marketplace. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. This notice is issued to help determine the appropriate acquisition method including small business socioeconomic set aside possibilities and to determine the availability of commercial or non-commercial companies technically capable of meeting the Government's potential requirement. It is not construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Furthermore, it should be noted that any future solicitations that may be issued as a result of this notice, or in response to this requirement, may be issued using a different solicitation number from the one identified above. Purpose NIH is seeking information from qualified R&D firms, small businesses, and subcontractors regarding their capabilities to support the operation, consolidation, and/or recompete of one or more NIH-funded biorepositories for FY 2028, including at a minimum the NIDA Center for Genetic Studies (NCGS) and the NIH Brain Development Cohorts (NBDC) Biobank, which supports the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, and HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study. Background NIH currently supports over 20 biorepositories across 10+ Institutes and Centers, with each individual biorepository storing several thousands to over 3.5 million samples. NIH biorepositories have stored, analyzed, and distributed millions of samples of biomaterials to enable broad investigations into the myriad of biological and environmental factors that affect health, development, and disease. Purpose NIH is seeking information from qualified R&D firms, small businesses, and subcontractors regarding their capabilities to support the operation, consolidation, and/or recompete of one or more NIH-funded biorepositories for FY 2028, including at a minimum the NIDA Center for Genetic Studies (NCGS) and the NIH Brain Development Cohorts (NBDC) Biobank, which supports the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, and HEALthy Brain and Child Development (HBCD) Study. This notice also serves to determine the availability of all small businesses (e.g., 8(a), Veteran-owned small businesses, service-disabled Veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, small disadvantaged businesses, and women-owned small businesses) with the capability to perform this work. Background NIH currently supports over 20 biorepositories across 10+ Institutes and Centers, with each individual biorepository storing several thousands to over 3.5 million samples. NIH biorepositories have stored, analyzed, and distributed millions of samples of biomaterials to enable broad investigations into the myriad of biological and environmental factors that affect health, development, and disease. These repositories typically: Receive, process, store, and biosamples from a wide range of biospecimen types (e.g. blood/derivatives, fluids, DNA/RNA, hair, cell lines, iPSCs, teeth, fecal matter, birth specimens and other tissues such as brain and other organs) at various temperature and storage conditions (e.g. -80C, liquid nitrogen; fresh, frozen, paraffin-embedded, formalin-fixed) at scales ranging from tens of thousands to several million specimens. title: Request for Information - Sentinel OMC Packages & OGF, Malmstrom Air Force Base, MT
description: 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market intelligence and acquisition planning purposes. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Qualifications (RFQ), or invitation for bid. No solicitation is currently available. Participation is strictly voluntary. The Government will not award any agreement or contract as a result of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. Submission of a response does not obligate the Government in any way and will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) or FAR-based small-business set-aside rules, the NAICS code above is provided for market-intelligence purposes to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base. 2. PURPOSE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, is conducting market intelligence to assess industry capability, capacity, interest, and feedback regarding the potential establishment of a multi-year, multi-party Other Transaction Authority (OTA) framework agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The framework would enable Seattle District to execute a multitude of OTA methods with multiple parties over numerous years, with individual projects or packages authorized through project orders. While the near-term primary focus is the Sentinel Operations and Maintenance Complex (OMC) packages (OMC includes Consolidated Maintenance Facility, Integrated Training Center, Missile Handling Center, and Integrated Command Center) and Operations Group Facility (OGF) at Malmstrom Air Force Base, the Government is also interested in industry feedback on a vehicle broad enough to support construction of numerous facilities at military installations under Seattle District�s area of responsibility. 3. PROJECT BACKGROUND � PRIMARY NEAR-TERM FOCUS The Sentinel (Ground Based Strategic Deterrent) program is modernizing the Nation�s land-based intercontinental ballistic missile force. At Malmstrom AFB, the Air Force is constructing a suite of new facilities collectively referred to as the OMC, together with the OGF. These facilities replace aging Minuteman III infrastructure and provide purpose-built command, maintenance, training, missile-handling, and operations capabilities for the Sentinel weapon system. Primary near-term facilities under consideration include (approximate sizes based on current planning data; final designs may vary): Consolidated Maintenance Facility (CMF) (Est. Magnitude: $200M-$300M) � Approximately 181,000 SF. Administrative offices, maintenance shops, drive-thru high bays with overhead cranes and vehicle exhaust systems sized for Transporter Erectors (TE), Payload Transporters (PT), and Missile Transporters (MT); vault and secure storage; loading dock and shipping/receiving areas. Integrated Training Center (ITC) (Est. Magnitude: $100M-$200M) � Approximately 77,000 SF. High-bay and single-story technical training labs, shops, and classrooms consolidating wing-level maintenance, security forces, cyber-defense, and operations training on Sentinel-unique systems and devices. Missile Handling Complex (MHC)(Est. Magnitude: $100M-$200M) � Two facilities totaling approximately 50,000 SF. Three-bay transfer facility with embedded rails for Sentinel missile handling and a companion three-bay facility for positioning and storage of mission-ready transporters/erectors. Integrated Command Center (ICC)(Est. Magnitude: $100M-$200M) � Centralized operations facility supporting day-to-day mission control, status and security monitoring, weapons-systems management, cyber defense, and real-time leadership situational awareness. Operations Group Facility (OGF)(Est. Magnitude: $200M-$300M) � Multi-story office and collaboration space supporting planning and operations functions, enhancing span of control, and providing associated support spaces (administrative, training, supply, and dispatch functions). Design for these packages is being performed by Jacobs Engineering under existing design contracts. Design maturity varies by package (35% to 95%, with a majority at 95% completion). The Air Force treats the OMC as one project under a single aggregated DD Form 1391. Utility Infrastructure, which serves the entire OMC campus, is currently being addressed under a separate OT method. (See Sam.gov Notice ID: W912DW26S1CE0, Title: Request for Information - Sentinel Utility Infrastructure, Malmstrom Air Force Base, MT). 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY � FRAMEWORK CONCEPT Seattle District is exploring the feasibility of establishing one large overarching Other Transaction agreement (or a limited number of agreements) under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a that would function as a flexible multi-year framework. Key characteristics under consideration include: Multi-year period of performance sufficient to support sequential and concurrent facility packages across the Sentinel beddown and related MILCON workload. It is anticipated to be approximately 5 years with the potential to extend to a total of 7 years. Multiple parties � Potential for single-agreement or multiple-agreement structure allowing the Government to select among qualified parties for individual project/sub-agreement opportunities. Multitude of OTA methods � Flexibility to apply Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk), Progressive Design-Build, construction-only collaborative approaches, or other commercially adapted methods on a project-by-project basis depending on design maturity, risk profile, and schedule drivers. Project orders � Individual work packages or scopes would be authorized through bilateral project orders that define scope, price (or GMP), schedule, and method, analogous to task/project orders under an overarching agreement. Geographic and mission flexibility � While Malmstrom Sentinel packages (OMC and OGF) are the immediate focus, the framework is considering the possibility/capability for other MILCON workload assigned to Seattle District (anticipated to cover areas across Washington, Montana, Idaho, and Oregon. Military Installations include but are not limited to: Malmstrom Air Force Base, Fairchild Air Force Base, Mountain Home Air Force Base, Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Air National Guard Sites). The Government seeks industry input on whether this type of multi-party, multi-method, multi-year OT framework is attractive and executable, what commercial terms would make it successful, and how best to structure competition, on-ramping, and project order competition or selection. 5. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are requested to submit responses by completing the online questionnaire at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/dnW9AUb6aj The questionnaire is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence and addresses industry capability, experience, technical capabilities, construction considerations, and recommended OTA and commercial practices. If necessary, interested parties may also submit a brief capabilities statement containing relevant information not otherwise addressed in the questionnaire. Capability statements shall not exceed 5 pages in length. The Government requests that firms avoid duplicating information already provided through the questionnaire. Supplemental capability statements are requested to be submitted via email to the individual(s) listed below no later than 10:00 AM Pacific Time on 20 October 2026. Late responses may still be considered at the Government�s discretion but are not guaranteed review prior to strategy finalization. Kyla Couch, Contract Specialist Military/Environmental/Interagency & International Services (IIS) Branch Contracting Division, Seattle District, Northwestern Division Email: kyla.m.couch@usace.army.mil Subject li

title: Natchez Trace Parkway Project MS NP NATR 3F26
description: Sealed bids from all business concerns will be accepted for the Natchez Trace Parkway, Project MS NP NATR 3F26, Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000001, located in Chickasaw County, Mississippi. The project consists of resurfacing the Parkway, including ramps, bridges, intersections and parking/pull-off areas. The work includes milling, asphalt overlay, shoulder widening, spot reconstruction, pavement markings, raised profile striping at bridge approaches, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $10,000,000 to $12,000,000. title: Ft Leavenworth Army Corrections Brigade Health & Comfort Items
description: INTRODUCTION The MICC-Fort Leavenworth, KS is issuing this source sought notice as a means of conducting market research to identify potential sources having an interest and industry product supply available to support/provide Health and Comfort Items for the Army Corrections Brigade (ACB) facilities at Fort Leavenworth Kansas. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform the services defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. BACKGOUND The United States Army Corrections Brigade (ACB), Fort Leavenworth, requires Health and Comfort Items located on Fort Leavenworth, KS. Services include all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, and supervision as defined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. Based on the responses to this source sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses (in full or in part) or procured through full and open competition. All small business set-aside categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding submissions. DISCLAIMER THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. ELIGIBILITY The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is (311919-Other Snack Food Manufacturing) with a Small Business Size Standard of (1,250 Employees). The Product Service Code (PSC) is (V003- Transportation/Travel/Relocation- Motor Pool and Packing/Crating: Packing/Crating). SUBMISSION DETAILS Interested businesses should submit a brief capabilities statement package (no more than ten 8.5 X 11 inch pages, font no smaller than 10 point) demonstrating ability to provide the products/systems listed in this Technical Description. Documentation should be in bullet format. No phone or email solicitations with regards to the status of the RFP will be accepted prior to its release. Your response to this Sources Sought, including any capabilities statement, shall be electronically submitted to the Contract Specialist, Roberto Yroz, in either Microsoft Word or Portable Document Format (PDF), via email roberto.c.yroz.civ@army.mil no later than 1:00 p.m. (CDT) on 20 October 2026 and reference this synopsis number in subject line of e-mail and on all enclosed documents. Information and materials submitted in response to this request WILL NOT be returned. DO NOT SUBMIT CLASSIFIED MATERIAL. If your organization has the potential capacity to provide the required products/systems, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, primary points of contact (POCs) and their email address, FAX, Web site address, telephone number, and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the requirements of this notice, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. (NOTE: In accordance with FAR 10.001(b), agencies should not request potential sources to submit more than the minimum information necessary.) All data received in response to this Sources Sought that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government.

title: Ft Leavenworth Army Corrections Brigade Health & Comfort Items
description: INTRODUCTION The MICC-Fort Leavenworth, KS is issuing this source sought notice as a means of conducting market research to identify potential sources having an interest and industry product supply available to support/provide Health and Comfort Items for the Army Corrections Brigade (ACB) facilities at Fort Leavenworth Kansas. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform the services defined in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) except for those items specified as Government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. BACKGOUND The United States Army Corrections Brigade (ACB), Fort Leavenworth, requires Health and Comfort Items located on Fort Leavenworth, KS. Services include all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, and supervision as defined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. Based on the responses to this source sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses (in full or in part) or procured through full and open competition. All small business set-aside categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding submissions. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. The Product Service Code (PSC) is (V003- Transportation/Travel/Relocation- Motor Pool and Packing/Crating: Packing/Crating). SUBMISSION DETAILS Interested businesses should submit a brief capabilities statement package (no more than ten 8.5 X 11 inch pages, font no smaller than 10 point) demonstrating ability to provide the products/systems listed in this Technical Description. Your response to this Sources Sought, including any capabilities statement, shall be electronically submitted to the Contract Specialist, Roberto Yroz, in either Microsoft Word or Portable Document Format (PDF), via email roberto.c.yroz.civ@army.mil no later than 1:00 p.m. (CDT) on 20 October 2026 and reference this synopsis number in subject line of e-mail and on all enclosed documents. Information and materials submitted in response to this request WILL NOT be returned. DO NOT SUBMIT CLASSIFIED MATERIAL. title: Espoon Asunnot Oy / Lasituskorjaukset
description: Espoon Asunnot Oy / Lasituskorjaukset Hankinnan kohteena on lasituskorjaukset Espoon Asunnot Oy:n omistamiin kiinteistöihin. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen alueeseen: etelä ja pohjoinen. Kumpaankin alueeseen valitaan 1 toimija. Tilaaja ei voi kertoa tarkkoja määriä ennalta eikä luvata tiettyä määrää töitä sopimusaikana. Hintalistojen määräkertoimet ovat ainoastaan tarjousten vertailua varten. Toteutettavat työt tehdään tarjotuilla yksikköhinnoilla. Sellaiset lasituskorjaukset, joille ei ole annettu yksikköhintaa, tarjotaan tapauskohtaisesti erikseen. Edullisimman tarjouksen tehnyt tarjoaja valitaan eteläiseen alueeseen ja toiseksi edullisimman tarjouksen tehnyt tarjoaja pohjoiseen alueeseen. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteenä olevassa tarjouspyynnössä ja palvelukuvauksessa.,
